target: tracker.sh supersede — refuses without a REF
cmd:
mkdir -p factory/specs; printf -- '---
id: 001
title: thing
status: built
---
body
' > factory/specs/001-a.md; source "$PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/lib/tracker.sh"; if ( tracker_supersede factory/specs/001-a.md me ) >/dev/null 2>&1; then EC=0; else EC=$?; fi; if ( tracker_supersede factory/specs/001-a.md me '' 'reason only' ) >/dev/null 2>&1; then E2=0; else E2=$?; fi; jq -n --argjson ec "$EC" --argjson e2 "$E2" --arg st "$(_tracker_field factory/specs/001-a.md status)" --arg by "$(_tracker_field factory/specs/001-a.md superseded_by)" '{ec: $ec, e2: $e2, st: $st, by: $by}'
_note: the citation is what makes `superseded` safe to unblock dependents against — a supersede with no ref would be an unfalsifiable claim, and the verification in _tracker_supersede_lands would have nothing to check. Requiring it at the entry point is why that function can assume a ref exists.
